name: Chiefdom
description: Political system organized around ranked leadership, kinship, tribute, redistribution, and chiefly authority.

name: City-state
description: Urban-centered polity exercising authority over a city and associated territory.

name: Kingdom
description: Polity organized around monarchical sovereignty, succession, court structures, and territorial authority.

name: Empire
description: Multi-territorial political system incorporating or subordinating distinct populations under an imperial structure.

name: Republic
description: Political system in which public authority is institutionally distinct from hereditary personal sovereignty.

name: Democratic system
description: Family of systems structuring collective authorization and participation in public decision-making.

name: Bureaucratic administration
description: Administrative system using specialized offices, records, procedures, delegated authority, and continuity.

name: Federation
description: Political system distributing authority between a central government and constituent polities.

name: Customary law
description: Normative system maintained through established practice, precedent, social memory, recognition, and sanction.

name: Religious law
description: Legal or normative system deriving rules and interpretive authority from religious traditions and institutions.

name: Common-law system
description: Legal tradition substantially structured through judicial decisions, precedent, interpretation, and enacted law.

name: Civil-law system
description: Legal tradition substantially organized through codified statutes and systematic legal doctrine.

name: Restorative justice
description: Justice practices emphasizing repair of harm, affected-party participation, accountability, and restoration.

name: Gift economy
description: Exchange system in which transfers can create obligation, reciprocity, prestige, alliance, or relationship.

name: Tribute system
description: Resource-transfer system in which subordinate persons or communities provide goods, labor, or wealth to dominant authority.

name: Market economy
description: Economic system in which exchange and allocation are substantially coordinated through markets and price signals.

name: Planned economy
description: Economic system in which significant production and allocation decisions are coordinated through deliberate planning institutions.

name: Commons governance
description: Collective resource-management system using rules for access, stewardship, monitoring, sanction, and distribution.

name: Guild system
description: Occupational system organizing membership, training, standards, mutual obligations, market access, and political influence.

name: Kinship system
description: System organizing descent, household membership, marriage, inheritance, obligation, identity, and social relationship.

name: Clan system
description: Social organization based on recognized descent, ancestry, alliance, shared identity, or related obligations.

name: Caste system
description: Hereditary or strongly bounded stratification governing status, occupation, marriage, interaction, and access.

name: Patronage network
description: Relationship system exchanging protection, access, office, resources, or status through personal or factional ties.

name: Mutual-aid system
description: Cooperative system through which participants pool resources, labor, risk, or support for shared benefit.

name: Oral tradition
description: Knowledge-transmission system relying substantially on memory, performance, repetition, apprenticeship, and narrative.

name: Apprenticeship system
description: Learning system transmitting practical knowledge through guided participation under experienced practitioners.

name: University system
description: Institutional system combining advanced teaching, credentialing, knowledge production, preservation, and professional formation.

name: Archive system
description: Preservation and retrieval system organizing records, metadata, custody, access, and historical memory.

name: Scientific peer review
description: Validation and communication mechanism in which research claims are evaluated by knowledgeable peers under defined norms.

name: Temple system
description: Institutional system organizing sacred space, ritual activity, personnel, offerings, resources, and participation.

name: Monastic system
description: Religious institutional system organized around disciplined communal or solitary practice, rules, property, education, and ritual.

name: Levy system
description: Military recruitment system drawing personnel from a population under political, customary, or contractual obligation.

name: Professional army
description: Military system based substantially on continuously organized personnel, training, command, logistics, and institutional service.

name: Mercenary system
description: Military labor system in which armed personnel or units serve primarily through contractual compensation.

name: Fortification network
description: Defensive system linking fortified places through geography, logistics, surveillance, communication, and strategy.

name: Irrigation system
description: Water-control system coordinating physical infrastructure, labor, allocation, maintenance, property, and governance.

name: Road network
description: Infrastructure system connecting places through engineered routes, maintenance, rights, logistics, and movement.

name: Telecommunications system
description: Technical network enabling information transfer through interoperating physical, protocol, organizational, and service components.

name: Supply chain system
description: Interdependent system of production, transport, storage, financing, information, procurement, and distribution.

name: Hospital system
description: Organized health-care system combining facilities, personnel, procedures, resources, records, and patient flows.

name: Public-health system
description: Population-level system for surveillance, prevention, sanitation, health promotion, intervention, and coordination.

name: Forest stewardship system
description: Resource-management system governing access, harvesting, regeneration, protection, and social obligations around forests.

name: Festival system
description: Recurring cultural system coordinating ritual, performance, exchange, identity, scheduling, and communal participation.

name: Organized-crime network
description: Clandestine system coordinating illicit markets, enforcement, finance, information, recruitment, and territorial or relational control.

name: Smuggling network
description: Covert movement system transferring people or goods across regulated boundaries through concealed logistics and intermediaries.

name: Black-market system
description: Exchange system operating outside or against formal legal restrictions, with its own prices, trust mechanisms, risks, and enforcement.

name: Bribery mechanism
description: Corruption mechanism in which value is transferred to influence the exercise of entrusted authority.

name: Nepotism mechanism
description: Preferential allocation mechanism in which kinship improperly influences access to office, resources, or opportunity.

name: Regulatory capture
description: Governance failure in which a regulated interest substantially redirects regulatory institutions toward its own interests.

name: State capture
description: Systemic corruption pattern in which private or factional interests substantially reshape public institutions, rules, or enforcement for their benefit.

name: Embezzlement mechanism
description: Diversion mechanism in which entrusted resources are appropriated contrary to their authorized purpose.

name: Information suppression
description: Mechanism through which relevant information is withheld, distorted, destroyed, or restricted to alter system behavior or accountability.
